business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Nabors owns and operates land-based and offshore platform drilling rigs and supplies performance software, tubular running services, managed pressure drilling, and drilling technologies across more than 20 countries.
quotes: Nabors owns and operates one of the world’s largest land-based drilling rig fleets and is a provider of offshore platform rigs in the United States and numerous international markets.
Nabors also supplies performance software, tubular running services, managed pressure drilling services and innovative technologies for both its own rig fleet and those operated by third parties.
With operations in over 20 countries, we are a global provider of drilling and drilling-related services for land-based and offshore oil and natural gas wells.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Through its Rig Technologies segment, primarily Canrig, Nabors manufactures and sells advanced rig components, robotic systems, and downhole tools, and provides aftermarket sales and services to domestic and international third-party customers.
quotes: Our Rig Technologies segment is primarily comprised of Canrig, which manufactures and sells advanced rig components including top drives, catwalks, wrenches, drawworks and other drilling related equipment such as robotic systems and downhole tools, which are installed on both onshore and offshore drilling rigs.
Rig Technologies also provides aftermarket sales and services for the installed base of its equipment.
NDS and Rig Technologies’ portfolio of services and capabilities are available to third-party customers both in domestic and international markets.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Nabors generates drilling revenue primarily under daywork contracts, alongside footage contracts, turnkey contracts, and additive charges for performance-enhancing services, software, and equipment.
quotes: Our drilling contracts are typically daywork contracts.

While daywork contracts represent the bulk of our relationships, we also have footage contracts (in which the drilling contractor is paid on the basis of a rate per foot drilled) and turnkey contracts (in which the drilling contractor is paid for drilling a well to a specified depth for a fixed price).
These additional products and services are additive to our rig charges.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 1A of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Drilling contracts are generally awarded through competitive bidding on single-well, multi-well, or term durations, and early termination or suspension can leave rigs idle without full compensation.
quotes: Our contracts for land-based and offshore drilling have durations that are single-well, multi-well or term.

Most of our single-well contracts are subject to termination by the customer on short notice, while multi-well contracts and term contracts may provide us with early termination compensation in certain circumstances.

The early termination or suspension of a contract may result in a rig being idle for an extended period of time, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 1A of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Nabors serves major international, national, and independent oil and gas companies, with Saudi Aramco accounting for 30%, 31%, and 26% of consolidated operating revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, primarily through the SANAD joint venture.
quotes: Our customers include major international, national and independent oil and gas companies.

One customer, Saudi Aramco, accounted for approximately 30%, 31% and 26% of our consolidated operating revenues during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, which operating revenues are primarily included in the results of our International Drilling reportable segment.
These contracts are primarily operated through SANAD, our joint venture with Saudi Aramco.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1A of the 2025 Form 10-K and Note [1] of the September 30, 2026 Form 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated in Nabors' largest contract drilling customers—accounting for 41%, 43%, and 37% of consolidated operating revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively—while related-party operating revenues totaled $0.9 billion in the 9 Months Ended Sep. 30, 2026.
quotes: In 2025, 2024 and 2023, we received approximately 41%, 43% and 37%, respectively, of our consolidated operating revenues from our three largest contract drilling customers (including their affiliates), with our largest customer and partner in our SANAD joint venture, Saudi Aramco, representing 30%, 31% and 26% of our consolidated operating revenues, respectively, for these periods.

Includes related party revenues of $0.3 billion and $0.9 billion for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively and $0.3 billion and $0.8 billion for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively.

business_model.claim: Nabors organizes its business into reportable segments consisting of U.S. Drilling, International Drilling, Drilling Solutions, and Rig Technologies.
quotes: Our business consists of four reportable segments: U.S. Drilling, International Drilling, Drilling Solutions and Rig Technologies.

Management evaluates the performance of our reportable segments using adjusted operating income (loss), which is our segment performance measure, because we believe that this financial measure reflects our ongoing profitability and performance.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 of the 2025 Form 10-K and Part I Item 2 of the September 30, 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Demand for Nabors' services and products depends on oil and gas companies' exploration, development, and production spending, which moves with volatile crude oil and natural gas prices, operator capital discipline, and U.S. producer consolidation.
quotes: To a large degree, our businesses depend on the level of capital spending by oil and gas companies for exploration, development and production activities.
The level of exploration, development and production activities is, to a large extent, tied to the prices of oil and natural gas, which can fluctuate significantly and are highly volatile.
Certain oil and gas producers may intentionally limit their capital spending as they focus on generating returns to shareholders as opposed to maximizing hydrocarbon production.
Further, significant industry consolidation, particularly among U.S. operators has occurred in recent years.

quotes: Daily rig revenue represents operating revenue, divided by the total number of revenue days during the quarter.

business_model.basis: Stated in Part I Item 2 of the September 30, 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: In the United States, continued gains in drilling efficiency enable producers to sustain output with fewer rigs, tempering rig-count demand even as leading-edge rig pricing rises.
quotes: Also in the United States, leading-edge rig pricing has continued to increase, supporting wider daily rig margins.
At the same time, continued gains in drilling efficiency have enabled U.S. oil and gas producers to sustain production levels with fewer rigs.
As a result, while rig pricing dynamics are improving, these efficiency gains have impacted the number of rigs required to sustain those production levels.

business_model.basis: Stated in Part I Item 2 of the September 30, 2026 Form 10-Q and the October 27, 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
business_model.claim: Middle East geopolitical disruptions and customer actions drive swings in international rig activity, including rig reactivations, SANAD's deployment of its 17th newbuild rig in Saudi Arabia, and recent SANAD rig suspensions.
quotes: During the first three quarters of 2026, the conflict in the Middle East resulted in damage to oil and gas production facilities in several producing countries and significant disruptions to regional oil and gas exports.
In the Middle East, a number of previously-suspended onshore and offshore rigs have been reactivated.
More recently, certain operators have taken measures to reduce near-term activity, including placing rigs on standby and issuing additional suspension notices.
The SANAD land drilling joint venture successfully deployed its 17th newbuild rig in Saudi Arabia.
We expect further margin improvement in the fourth quarter, despite a lower SANAD rig count following the suspension of five rigs.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Seasonal weather reduces second-quarter drilling activity and financial results in Alaska due to the annual spring thaw and can disrupt U.S. offshore Gulf of America operations during summer tropical weather.
quotes: Specifically, our drilling operations in Alaska generally experience reduced levels of activity and financial results during the second quarter of each year, due to the annual spring thaw.
In addition, our U.S. offshore market can be impacted during summer months by tropical weather systems in the Gulf of America.
Our overall financial results reflect the seasonal variations experienced in these operations, but seasonality does not materially impact the remaining portions of our business.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 7 of the 2025 Form 10-K and Part I Item 2 of the September 30, 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Acquisitions and divestitures materially reshape segment revenues: the March 11, 2025 Parker Drilling merger added U.S. offshore, Alaska, international, and Drilling Solutions revenues, whereas the August 20, 2025 sale of Quail Tools reduced Drilling Solutions revenue by $25.9 million, or 18%, year-over-year in the three months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: On March 11, 2025, Nabors completed its merger with Parker Drilling Company (“Parker”) resulting in Parker becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of Nabors.
Incremental revenue from acquired Parker rig operations in international markets and the contribution of recently deployed rigs in other international markets comprise the majority of the increase.
On August 20, 2025, Nabors entered into a definitive agreement to sell Quail Tools to Superior Energy Services, Inc.
Operating revenues for this segment decreased by $25.9 million or 18% during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the corresponding prior year period.
The decrease is primarily attributable to operating revenue from Quail Tools, LLC, which is included in the activity for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1A of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Operating expenses contain fixed costs such as depreciation and regional support operations that do not decline proportionally with lower rig utilization or dayrates.
quotes: Our operating expense includes all direct and indirect costs associated with the operation, maintenance and support of our drilling and related equipment, many of which are not affected by changes in dayrates and some of which are not affected by utilization.
During periods of reduced revenues or activity, certain of our fixed costs (such as depreciation) may not decline and often we may incur additional costs.

During times of reduced utilization, reductions in costs may not be immediate as we may not be able to fully reduce the cost of our support operations in a particular geographic region due to the need to support the remaining drilling rigs in that region.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 7 of the 2025 Form 10-K and Part I Item 2 of the September 30, 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: General and administrative and depreciation expenses are driven by workforce size, operating activity, inflation, capital expenditures, and acquisitions or divestitures, rising by $55.3 million and $15.8 million, respectively, in 2025 following the Parker acquisition.
quotes: General and administrative expenses in 2025 totaled $304.6 million, representing an increase of $55.3 million, or 22% from 2024.
This is reflective of increases in workforce costs and general operating costs as a result of the Parker acquisition, along with inflationary pressures as market conditions have changed.
Depreciation and amortization expense in 2025 was $649.2 million, representing an increase of $15.8 million, or 2%, from 2024.
The increase is a result of the additional assets obtained in the Parker acquisition.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1A of the 2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Component and raw material costs and operational continuity depend on a limited set of third-party suppliers and international trade policies, including U.S. tariffs and foreign retaliatory tariffs.
quotes: Certain components, parts and equipment that we use in our operations may be available only from a small number of suppliers, manufacturers or service providers.

While the impact of such measures, both pending and threatened, remains uncertain, these measures could increase the cost of components and raw materials in our supply chain and, consequently, our costs.
We may not be able to pass along these increased costs to our customers.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 7 of the 2025 Form 10-K and Part I Item 2 of the September 30, 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Debt balances and effective interest rates drive material interest expense, which totaled $215.4 million in 2025 before declining 23%, or $12.2 million, year-over-year to $42.1 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026 as average debt fell.
quotes: Interest expense for 2025 was $215.4 million, representing an increase of $4.5 million, or 2%, compared to 2024.
The increase was primarily due to an increase in our effective interest rate levels and an increase in our average outstanding debt balance throughout 2025 as compared to 2024.
Interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $42.1 million, representing a decrease of $12.2 million, or 23%, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.
The decrease was primarily due to a decrease in our average outstanding debt balance throughout the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

With operations in over 20 countries, we are a global provider of drilling and drilling-related services for land-based and offshore oil and natural gas wells.
242 actively marketed rigs for land-based drilling operations in the United States and multiple international markets; and
27 actively marketed rigs for offshore platform drilling operations in the United States and various countries throughout the world.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and the 3Q 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Management believes Nabors deploys the most capable and modern rig fleet in the Lower 48 market, where average rigs working grew to 72.8 in the third quarter of 2026 from 59.2 in the prior-year period.
quotes: We believe we deploy the most capable and modern rig fleet in the Lower 48 market.
U.S. Drilling adjusted EBITDA increased to $99 million from $94 million in the second quarter.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
competitive_position.claim: Nabors differentiates its rigs by integrating proprietary downhole hardware, automation, performance software, tubular running services, and managed pressure drilling, while also selling equipment and services to third-party customers.
quotes: One key component of Nabors’ strategy is to seamlessly integrate downhole hardware, surface equipment and software solutions into rig designs that drive industry-leading performance and increasing efficiencies.
We integrate our TRS and MPD into the rig, eliminating the need for third party service providers and thereby improving efficiencies and reducing costs.
NDS and Rig Technologies’ portfolio of services and capabilities are available to third-party customers both in domestic and international markets.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and the 3Q 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Nabors evidenced technological traction by introducing the PACE-X Ultra rig in 2025, securing new RZR rig floor automation commitments in the third quarter of 2026, and achieving a 27,600 feet in 148 hours drilling record in North Dakota.
quotes: In 2025, we introduced our PACE®-X Ultra rig, an upgrade to our PACE®-X800 rig.
Canrig secured commitments for four additional RZR™ rig floor automation modules, which will bring the total deployed to six.
A PACE®-B rig in North Dakota achieved an impressive drilling performance of more than 27,600 feet in 148 hours, with an average rate of penetration of nearly 187 feet per hour.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: International Drilling reached a record daily adjusted gross margin of $19,060 in the third quarter of 2026, up $1,526 or 8.7% sequentially, supported by improved pricing and high-margin rig deployments.
quotes: International Drilling daily adjusted gross margin reached a record $19,060, up $1,526, or 8.7%, sequentially.
Strong field performance across multiple countries and high-margin rig deployments drove the increase.

The increase is primarily attributable to a 6% increase in the average rigs working, reflecting increased drilling activity, along with improved pricing, as market conditions and demand for our international drilling services have increased since the prior year.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Nabors identifies its safety record as a competitive advantage in winning job awards, supported by Rig Zone Robotics and Red Zone Management technologies.
quotes: In addition, an important factor in determining job awards is our ability to maintain a strong safety record.
In addition, our safety record is a competitive advantage for us and if one or more incidents were to occur it could significantly affect this advantage.

We deploy innovative solutions, including the RZR system, to reduce exposure to high-risk situations, as well as the use of advanced analytics, machine learning based advisory tools, and computer vision technology for Red Zone Management.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: A core threat to Nabors' competitive position is excess industry drilling capacity combined with mobile rigs that can shift between regions and intensify price competition.
quotes: The oilfield services industry is very competitive with a significant amount of excess capacity.

Rigs and drilling-related equipment can be moved from one region to another in response to changes in levels of activity and market conditions, which may result in an oversupply of such rigs and drilling-related equipment in certain areas, and accordingly, increased price competition.

We believe that competitive pricing is a significant factor in determining which service provider is awarded a job in these markets and customers are increasingly sensitive to pricing during periods of market instability.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and the 3Q 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: Nabors faces acute customer concentration risk, as its three largest customers generated 41% of 2025 consolidated operating revenues—including 30% from Saudi Aramco, its SANAD joint venture partner.
quotes: In 2025, 2024 and 2023, we received approximately 41%, 43% and 37%, respectively, of our consolidated operating revenues from our three largest contract drilling customers (including their affiliates), with our largest customer and partner in our SANAD joint venture, Saudi Aramco, representing 30%, 31% and 26% of our consolidated operating revenues, respectively, for these periods.
Replacing significant customers is difficult, and it is unlikely we would be able to replace such a loss in revenue from a single or a few larger customers, especially Saudi Aramco.
We expect further margin improvement in the fourth quarter, despite a lower SANAD rig count following the suspension of five rigs.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Contracts with state-owned energy companies and local joint venture requirements expose Nabors to non-negotiable terms, local content mandates, termination without cause, and partner disputes.
quotes: The terms of these contracts may contain non-negotiable provisions and may expose us to greater commercial, political, operational and other risks than we assume in other contracts.

Much of the world’s oil and natural gas reserves are controlled by NOCs, which may require their contractors to meet local content requirements or other local standards, such as conducting our operations through joint ventures with local partners, that could be difficult or undesirable for us to meet.

Actions of and disputes with our joint venture partners could have a material adverse effect on the business and results of operations of our joint ventures and, in turn, our business and consolidated results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and the 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Demand for Nabors' services is threatened by oil and natural gas price volatility, producer capital discipline, customer consolidation, and drilling efficiency gains that reduce the number of rigs needed.
quotes: A decrease or prolonged decline in the price of oil or natural gas or in the exploration, development and production activities of our customers could result in a corresponding decline in the demand for our services or a reduction in dayrates and utilization, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations and cash flows.
Certain oil and gas producers may intentionally limit their capital spending as they focus on generating returns to shareholders as opposed to maximizing hydrocarbon production.
Further, significant industry consolidation, particularly among U.S. operators has occurred in recent years.
At the same time, continued gains in drilling efficiency have enabled U.S. oil and gas producers to sustain production levels with fewer rigs.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Customer contracts can be terminated on short notice for single-well work, or renegotiated, suspended, or terminated without full early-termination compensation during downturns.
quotes: Most of our single-well contracts are subject to termination by the customer on short notice, while multi-well contracts and term contracts may provide us with early termination compensation in certain circumstances.
In addition, some contracts may be suspended, rather than terminated early, for an extended period of time, in some cases without adequate, or any, compensation.

During periods of depressed market conditions, we may be subject to an increased risk of our customers, including government-controlled entities, seeking to renegotiate, repudiate or terminate their contracts and/or to otherwise exert commercial influence to our disadvantage.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and the 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Fixed costs such as depreciation and regional support limit expense flexibility when rig utilization falls, while the 2025 sale of Quail Tools reduced Drilling Solutions revenue by 18% year over year in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: During periods of reduced revenues or activity, certain of our fixed costs (such as depreciation) may not decline and often we may incur additional costs.

Accordingly, a decline in revenues due to lower dayrates or utilization may not be offset by a corresponding decrease in drilling services and solutions expense, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Operating revenues for this segment decreased by $25.9 million or 18% during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the corresponding prior year period.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: Emerging drilling or alternative green technologies could erode the competitiveness of Nabors' fleet and require higher capital spending, while intellectual property enforcement limits could diminish competitive advantages.
quotes: The development of new technologies or the discovery of alternative green technologies may cause our drilling methods and equipment to become less competitive, and it may become necessary to incur higher levels of operating and capital expenditures in order to keep pace with the disruptive trends in the drilling industry.
Limitations on our ability to obtain, maintain, protect or enforce our intellectual property rights, including our trade secrets, could cause a loss in revenues and any competitive advantage we hold.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors, Item 7 MD&A, and the 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Global operations and supply chains face threats from Middle East conflict disruptions, 2025 U.S. and retaliatory tariffs, supplier concentration, and sanctions linked to $26.5 million of Russia asset impairments in 2025.
quotes: For instance, in 2025 the United States proposed and instituted numerous trade policies—including the termination of trade agreements, imposition of ad valorum tariffs on certain imports into the United States, and other regulations affecting trade between the United States and countries in which we conduct business and source components.
Certain components, parts and equipment that we use in our operations may be available only from a small number of suppliers, manufacturers or service providers.

During 2025, this loss was from $26.5 million in asset impairments related to assets held in Russia, $19.9 million of transaction related costs, $24.6 million related to severance and reorganization costs, $15.5 million for losses on debt buybacks, and $15.2 million in other than temporary impairment of securities which was offset by $8.4 million of mark-to-market gains on the common share warrants and $46.9 million in gain on sales of assets.

During the first three quarters of 2026, the conflict in the Middle East resulted in damage to oil and gas production facilities in several producing countries and significant disruptions to regional oil and gas exports.
